summary: Australia's Office of Impact Analysis recommends a Value of a Statistical Life Year of A$245,000 in 2024 dollars, roughly USD 162,000, as a per-life-year anchor.
label_raw: VLY (Value of a Statistical Life Year): A$245,000 (2024 dollars), 3% discount rate
source_citation: Office of Impact Analysis, Guidance Note: Value of Statistical Life (Nov 2024) (A$245,000 per statistical life year in 2024 dollars, 3% private time-preference discount rate); A$245,000 ÷ 1.516 IRS 2024 avg AUD/USD ≈ USD 162,000. https://oia.pmc.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-11/value-statistical-life-guidance-note.pdf

summary: Australia's Office of Impact Analysis recommends a Value of Statistical Life of A$5.7 million in 2024 dollars, roughly USD 3.76 million.
label_raw: VSL: A$5.7M (2024 dollars), OIA recommended value, 3% discount rate
source_citation: Office of Impact Analysis, Guidance Note: Value of Statistical Life (Nov 2024), p.2 (A$5.7M VSL in 2024 dollars via ABS Wage Price Index, underlying Abelson 2007, 3% private time-preference discount rate); A$5.7M ÷ 1.516 IRS 2024 avg AUD/USD ≈ USD 3.76M. https://oia.pmc.gov.au/sites/default/files/2024-11/value-statistical-life-guidance-note.pdf ; https://oia.pmc.gov.au/resources/guidance-assessing-impacts/value-statistical-life

summary: Canada's Treasury Board mandates a Value of Statistical Life of C$6.11 million in 2004 dollars for federal cost-benefit analysis, about USD 6.9 million when inflated to 2024 dollars.
label_raw: VSL: C$6.11M (2004 dollars), federal CBA mandated value
source_citation: Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat, Canadian Cost-Benefit Analysis Guide: Regulatory Proposals (VSL C$6.11M, departments adjust for inflation via StatCan CPI); 2004 to 2024 CPI ~x1.55 ≈ C$9.5M ÷ 1.370 IRS 2024 avg CAD/USD ≈ USD 6.9M. https://www.tbs-sct.canada.ca/rtrap-parfa/analys/analys-eng.pdf ; https://www.canada.ca/en/treasury-board-secretariat/services/federal-regulatory-management/guidelines-tools/policy-cost-benefit-analysis.html

summary: The European Commission estimates the average statistical value of a life for the EU27+UK at EUR 4.7 million (2024 prices), roughly USD 5.09 million in 2024 dollars.
source_citation: EUROCONTROL, Standard Inputs for Economic Analyses §44 Value of a Statistical Life, citing European Commission DG MOVE Handbook on the External Costs of Transport (2019), adjusted to 2024 prices. https://ansperformance.eu/economics/cba/standard-inputs/latest/chapters/value_of_a_statistical_life-vsl.html

summary: An academic stated-preference choice experiment puts Japan's Value of Statistical Life at JPY 350 million in 2002 yen, roughly USD 2.31 million in 2024 dollars, an upper-bound cross-check above the Cabinet Office figure.
source_citation: Japanese choice-experiment / stated-preference literature as summarized in OECD, Mortality Risk Valuation in Environment, Health and Transport Policies (2012) (VSL ¥350M in 2002 yen, ≈ US$2.9M at 2002 rates); nominal ¥350M ÷ 151.353 IRS 2024 avg JPY/USD ≈ USD 2.31M. https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2012/02/mortality-risk-valuation-in-environment-health-and-transport-policies_g1g1690a/9789264130807-en.pdf ; JSCE meta-analysis https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jscejj/79/20/79_23-20008/_article/-char/en

summary: Japan's Cabinet Office values a per-fatality human loss at JPY 226.07 million (a 2007-era willingness-to-pay estimate), roughly USD 1.65 million in 2024 dollars after modest inflation.
label_raw: Value of human life loss (死亡損失): JPY 226.07M (¥2億2,607万円), Cabinet Office WTP study
source_citation: Cabinet Office of Japan (内閣府), 交通事故の被害・損失の経済的分析に関する調査研究報告書 (per-fatality human loss JPY 226.07M via contingent-valuation WTP survey; adopted by MLIT for public-works appraisal). Face value ¥226.07M ÷ 151.353 IRS 2024 avg JPY/USD ≈ USD 1.49M; escalated to 2024 (~¥250M) ≈ USD 1.65M. https://www8.cao.go.jp/koutu/chou-ken/19html/houkoku.html ; https://www.mlit.go.jp/tec/hyouka/public/pdf_kentoukai03/04.pdf

summary: New Zealand's Transport Agency (Waka Kotahi) values a statistical life at NZ$12.5 million at July 2021 prices, roughly USD 8.95 million when escalated to 2024 dollars (about USD 7.56 million at the stated 2021 price basis).
label_raw: VoSL: NZ$12.5M (July 2021 prices), road-transport appraisal value
source_citation: NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi, Monetised Benefits and Costs Manual v1.6 (April 2023, carried in v1.7.x 2024); VoSL raised from NZ$4.88M to NZ$12.5M (2020-21 survey of ~8,000 New Zealanders). NZ$12.5M (2021) ÷ 1.654 IRS 2024 avg NZD/USD ≈ USD 7.56M; escalated to 2024 (NZ CPI ~x1.18 ≈ NZ$14.8M) ÷ 1.654 ≈ USD 8.95M. https://www.nzta.govt.nz/resources/monetised-benefits-and-costs-manual ; https://www.greaterauckland.org.nz/2023/05/04/new-values-of-time-and-life/

summary: The UK Department for Transport values preventing a single road fatality at about GBP 2.0 million (2022 prices), roughly USD 2.55 million in 2024 dollars.
label_raw: Value of Preventing a Fatality (VPF): GBP 2.0M (~2022 prices)
source_citation: UK Department for Transport, TAG Unit A4.1 — Social Impact Appraisal, Nov 2022, §2.2 (base value GBP 1M in 1997 prices, indexed to GDP per head); current values in the TAG Data Book. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/63a32a8d8fa8f539198d9bf3/TAG_Unit_A4.1_-_Social-impact-appraisal_Nov_2022_Accessible_v1.0.pdf.pdf ; https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/tag-data-book
